page.overview:
What is Mordor?

Mordor was a black, volcanic plain in the southeast of Middle-earth, east of Gondor, Ithilien, and the great river Anduin. In the Second Age, Mordor was chosen by Sauron as his realm due to its three sides guarded by mountain ranges, creating a natural fortress, preventing any from easily invading it.

The large mountain ranges protecting Mordor were arranged roughly in a rectangular manner: the Ered Lithui ('Ash Mountains') to the north, and the Ephel Dúath ('Mountains of Shadow') to the west and south. In the northwest corner of Mordor, the deep valley of Udûn was one of the few entrances for large armies. Guarding the outer entrance was the Black Gate. Outside it was the Dagorlad or "Battle Plain". Sauron's main fortress of Barad-dûr sat at the end of a spur of the Ered Lithui. To the southwest of Barad-dûr lay the arid Plateau of Gorgoroth and Mount Doom; to its east lay the plain of Lithlad.

Mordor's geography was excellent for defence against enemies attacking on all fronts, as nearly unscalable mountains defended Mordor on three sides, while the broken, jagged land of Gorgoroth and Núrn would greatly impede any army that managed to break through. Aside from its distant, eastern border, Mordor's only exit less fortified than the Black Gate was through the Morgul Pass and Cirith Ungol. Isildur originally built the city of Minas Ithil to guard the western end of both passes from any threat from Mordor, but in the Third Age, the population of the city waned, and it was conquered by the Nazgûl. It became the home of the Ringwraiths and was renamed Minas Morgul, thereafter a great stronghold of evil, ever at war with Gondor to the west until the end of the War of the Ring. To escape the vigilance of Morgul, to enter Mordor one still had to get past the lair of Shelob and the Tower of Cirith Ungol — a feat only Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee (led by Gollum) ever accomplished — though not without being waylaid by Shelob, and Frodo being taken prisoner to the Tower of Cirith Ungol.

The southern part of Mordor, called Núrn, was slightly more fertile, watered enough to hold the inland Sea of Núrnen. Núrn was made somewhat fertile because the ash blown from Mount Doom left its soil nutrient-rich, thus allowing dry-land farming.

connections.name: Nazgûl
connections.short_description: The Nazgûl (Black Speech for "Ringwraiths") or Úlairi (Quenya), also known as the Black Riders or The Nine, were the dreaded ring-servants of the Dark Lord Sauron in Middle-earth throughout the Second and Third Ages,…
